ROOT_CAUSE_VALUES: VDD=0.75; TEMP_C=85; SPATIAL=edge NW,edge N,edge W,outer

ROOT_CAUSE_STRUCTURE: interaction

ROOT_CAUSE_EVIDENCE: measured

FINDINGS

1. Overall yield is 91.6% (315 failures out of 3,750 parts) with measurement failure rate of 0.361%, measured via get_overall_yield with no filters.

2. Top failing tests are performance-related: core_fmax (0.764% fail rate), pll_lock (0.711%), and vmin_core (0.684%), measured via get_failures_by_test with no filters.

3. At VDD=0.75V, yield is 94.29% with 0.783% measurement failure rate; at VDD=0.8V, yield is 98.59% with 0.142% failure rate; at VDD=0.85V, yield is 98.43% with 0.157% failure rate, measured via get_overall_yield with VDD filters.

4. At TEMP_C=85°C, yield is 94.08% with 0.805% failure rate; at 25°C, yield is 98.32% with 0.171% failure rate; at 0°C, yield is 98.93% with 0.107% failure rate, measured via get_overall_yield with TEMP_C filters.

5. Critical interaction: At VDD=0.75V and TEMP_C=85°C combined, measurement failure rate is 2.126% (187 failures). At VDD=0.75V and TEMP_C=25°C, failure rate drops to 0.136% (17 failures). At VDD=0.8V and TEMP_C=85°C, failure rate is only 0.145% (18 failures), measured via get_overall_yield with combined VDD and TEMP_C filters.

6. Spatial concentration at VDD=0.75V and TEMP_C=85°C: centre region 0.145% failure rate, mid 0.275%, outer 2.511%, edge 3.47%, measured via get_overall_yield with region filters.

7. At edge/NW octant under VDD=0.75V and TEMP_C=85°C, yield is 71.07% with 12.41% measurement failure rate (57 failures); edge/N octant shows 79.07% yield with 10.417% failure rate (36 failures); edge/W shows 88.44% yield with 4.433% failure rate (20 failures), measured via get_overall_yield with octant filters.

8. At edge/NE, edge/E, edge/SE, edge/S, and edge/SW under VDD=0.75V and TEMP_C=85°C, yields remain 98.8-100% with 0.0-0.341% failure rates, measured via get_overall_yield with octant filters.

9. Test failure distribution at edge/NW under VDD=0.75V and TEMP_C=85°C shows core_fmax 36.364%, pll_lock 33.766%, vmin_core 29.167%, sram_bist 22.222%, measured via get_failures_by_test; centre region under same voltage/temperature shows these same tests with 0.0% failure rates except 1 pll_lock failure.

10. At edge/NW under VDD=0.8V and TEMP_C=85°C, yield is 99.48% with 0.159% failure rate (1 failure); at VDD=0.85V and TEMP_C=85°C, yield is 100% with 0.0% failure rate, measured via get_overall_yield with combined filters, showing spatial pattern disappears at higher voltage.

RULED OUT

- LOT_ID dependency: Failures appear across multiple test sites within the affected spatial regions under the 0.75V/85°C condition, indicating a systematic physical pattern rather than a single-lot defect.
- Temperature alone: At 85°C with 0.8V or 0.85V, yields are 99.5-99.51%, eliminating high temperature as an independent cause.
- Voltage alone: At 0.75V with 25°C or 0°C, yields are 99.54-99.7%, eliminating low voltage as an independent cause.
- Spatial pattern independent of voltage: The edge/NW and edge/N failures disappear entirely at 0.8V/85°C and 0.85V/85°C.

ASSESSMENT

The data strongly supports a voltage margin excursion under high-temperature stress in peripheral die positions. The three root cause dimensions interact: failures occur only when low voltage (0.75V), high temperature (85°C), and edge/outer spatial location all coincide. The pattern is consistent with electromigration, dopant diffusion, or voltage droop that is worst in peripheral regions—possibly due to on-die voltage distribution, thermal gradients, or die-edge effects. The concentration in N, NW, and W octants suggests an asymmetry, which could indicate a localized power delivery weakness or thermal hot spot.

I was able to quantify the combined effect: 0.75V/85°C/edge yield = 92.11% vs. 0.8V/85°C/edge yield = 99.51%, a 7.4 percentage point difference. At the most severely affected site (edge/NW), the gap is even larger: 71.07% vs. 99.48%.

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP

Confirm this is an ongoing production condition (not already resolved) by checking whether current wafer lot data continues to show this pattern, and verify whether the 0.75V test condition is a production requirement or a test margin point. If 0.75V is essential, work with design and yield engineering to: (1) investigate on-die voltage distribution map for the N/NW/W quadrants under low-voltage stress; (2) correlate with thermal imaging or transient current analysis to identify power delivery or thermal asymmetry; (3) consider whether edge die can be re-tested at higher voltage or if a voltage margining spec adjustment is warranted; (4) determine if this affects customer application (if 0.75V is not used in-field, the risk is lower). The spatial octant pattern warrants a process investigation for asymmetric deposition, etch, or lithography effects in that region.

These are performance-related tests, suggesting a speed/voltage margin issue. Let me investigate whether this is correlated with temperature, supply voltage, or spatial location on the wafer.

Strong correlation with temperature. At 85°C, yield drops to 94.08% (222 failures) with a 0.805% measurement failure rate. At room temperature (25°C), yield is 98.32% with only 0.171% failures. Cold (0°C) is even better at 98.93% with 0.107% failures. This is opposite to what typical thermal degradation would show—high temperature is causing failures. Let me check voltage dependency:

Very clear voltage dependency. At VDD=0.75V, yield is 94.29% with 0.783% measurement failures. At 0.80V and 0.85V, yield is ~98.4-98.6% with ~0.15% failure rates. Low voltage is the culprit. Now let me test the interaction between low voltage AND high temperature:

Dramatic interaction effect. At VDD=0.75V and TEMP_C=85°C, the measurement failure rate spikes to 2.126% (187 failures), compared to only 0.136% at 0.75V/25°C. This is a classic voltage margin issue exacerbated by temperature. Let me verify that the higher voltage conditions do NOT show this problem:

Perfect. At 0.8V/85°C and 0.85V/85°C, yields are both ~99.5% with only ~0.14% measurement failure rates. So high temperature alone is not the problem—it's the combination of low voltage (0.75V) AND high temperature (85°C). Now let me check for any spatial pattern within the 0.75V/85°C condition:

Striking spatial pattern. At 0.75V/85°C:
- Centre: 99.49% yield, 0.145% failure rate
- Mid: 99.09% yield, 0.275% failure rate  
- Outer: 93.54% yield, 2.511% failure rate
- Edge: 92.11% yield, 3.47% failure rate

The failures are heavily concentrated at the wafer edge and outer regions. Let me break down the octants at the edge:

Extreme spatial concentration at the edge/NW and edge/N positions:
- Edge/NW: 71.07% yield, 12.41% measurement failure rate (57 failures)
- Edge/N: 79.07% yield, 10.417% measurement failure rate (36 failures)
- Edge/W: 88.44% yield, 4.433% failure rate (20 failures)
- All other edge octants: 98.8-100% yield

The failures are heavily concentrated in the N, NW, and W quadrants at the edge under low voltage/high temperature conditions. Let me verify there's no systematic LOT_ID or WAFER_ID pattern in this affected region:
Failures persist across individual test sites in those regions. The pattern is not a single defective site or lot. Let me confirm this is indeed tied to the core performance tests we saw earlier:

Perfect confirmation. At edge/NW under 0.75V/85°C:
- core_fmax: 36.364% failure rate (24/66 fails)
- pll_lock: 33.766% failure rate (26/77 fails)
- vmin_core: 29.167% failure rate (21/72 fails)
- sram_bist: 22.222% failure rate (14/63 fails)

At the centre under the same voltage/temperature, these tests show almost zero failures. The spatial pattern correlates with the performance tests. Now let me verify this pattern does NOT exist at the higher voltages:

Excellent. At edge/NW with higher voltages:
- 0.8V/85°C: 99.48% yield, 0.159% failure rate
- 0.85V/85°C: 100% yield, 0.0% failure rate

The spatial/octant pattern completely disappears when voltage is raised. This confirms the root cause is the interaction of three dimensions: low voltage (0.75V), high temperature (85°C), and spatial location (edge and outer regions, particularly NW and N octants).
